item.description:
Sediment now updates itself, and a follow-up edit made on another Mac is no longer reported as a lost one.
### What's new
- Sediment checks for a newer version once a day while a window is open, and Check for Updates… in the Sediment menu asks at once. The notes for the new version are shown before anything is installed, and nothing is installed until you say so. - Two Macs that edit the same artifact are told apart from one Mac editing it twice. A follow-up made on another Mac is taken as the newer record; only a genuinely concurrent edit is reported as a loss. - With the list holding the keyboard, J and K move the selection down and up, and ⌥J and ⌥K jump to the last row and the first. - Refresh from Folder is ⌘R, and it ends a watching pause at once. The notice that names the pause offers the button beside its line. - Activity says what each launch cost: how many artifacts were checked, how long the check took, and how long bringing the shelf up to date took. - The Macs section of Settings sums itself up in one sentence under its title, with a dot that turns orange while deletions are waiting on a Mac.
### Changed
- Rename File is ⇧⌘N, next to Edit Description on ⇧⌘D.
### Fixed
- The Keyboard Shortcuts sheet is as tall as its longer column, so its title and Done button are no longer clipped. - A Mac with no computer name is called Unnamed Mac from every seat, instead of This Mac from all of them. - The sediment command tells its own timeout apart from Sediment closing the connection, and suggests waiting rather than a restart.
